title: Shakur Stevenson signs with Zuffa Boxing in multifight deal
content:
Four-division world champion Shakur Stevenson has signed a multifight deal with TKO’s Zuffa Boxing promotion, both sides confirmed Thursday. The signing is Zuffa’s biggest yet and comes just over a year since the fledgling promotion’s launch under UFC head Dana White and Saudi investor Turki Al-Sheikh.

Stevenson, the current WBO 140-pound champion, said in an interview with The Athletic that he won’t be disclosing the details of the deal because he doesn’t “want anyone in my pockets.” It’s unclear with whom he’ll share a ring first and at what weight he will fight, though Zuffa said it will share more about its plans in the coming weeks.

“Shakur is one of the best pound-for-pound fighters in the world. He’s 29 years old, undefeated and already a four-division world champion,” White, who also is Zuffa Boxing co-founder, said in a statement. “This is a massive signing for Zuffa Boxing, and I’m looking forward to promoting this next fight.”

Stevenson is still unsure what the Zuffa signing means for his WBO title, which he won in dominant fashion over Teofimo Lopez in January at Madison Square Garden. The fight ended in a unanimous decision in Stevenson’s favor, putting his professional record at 25-0. Zuffa has no 140-pound weight class.

“I don’t really know yet. I’d love to keep my belt, but that’s up to the WBO. They gotta decide that and stick with it, unlike the WBC,” Stevenson said, referencing that sanctioning body’s decision to strip him of its lightweight world championship in February. Stevenson won that title in 2023 and defended it three times.

In addition to the WBC lightweight belt and his current WBO title, the 29-year-old southpaw from Newark, N.J., has held the WBC super featherweight championship and the WBO’s featherweight and super featherweight championships. As an amateur, Stevenson won a silver medal at bantamweight during the 2016 Rio Olympics.

Asked who is on his wish list at the moment, Stevenson smiled and said he’s not worried about the current lineup Zuffa has assembled. He dismissed previous callouts by the likes of Jose El Rayo Valenzuela, who said last week he wants to face Stevenson next.

“There was nobody on this roster that I saw and thought, ‘I want to get in the ring with that guy.’ I’m looking for the biggest fights we can make. If it’s a big enough fight, we’re gonna make it happen,” Stevenson said. “There’s no way I’m going to fight him.”

Stevenson was equally unbothered by White’s goal of keeping all Zuffa fights in-house, though he did not say whether his contract includes guaranteed freedom to take on boxers under other sanctioning bodies or promotions.

The boxing community’s list of dream fights for Stevenson has grown as he’s compiled accolades, with stars such as Devin Haney, Gervonta “Tank” Davis and Ryan Garcia among the top names. None of those fighters is on the Zuffa roster, but Stevenson reiterated he’s not worried about exclusivity issues and is confident Zuffa will help him maximize his opportunities.

“I’d love to face Ryan. He’s still got a little ‘chip,’ supposedly, from when I beat him in the amateurs. Like, come on, bro, it was 10 years ago, move on. It’s pro now. But definitely open to making that happen,” he told The Athletic. “Tank is still a fight everyone wants, and it’s definitely still something I’d do.

“I want all the big fights,” he continued. “If there’s one they can make, let’s do it. Whether that’s Devin Haney, Tank, whoever.”

Stevenson also downplayed the hostile rhetoric White has lobbed at boxing’s longtime institutions and decision-makers. He said he’s never watched any events from UFC, which TKO also owns, but is now building a relationship with White and already has a yearslong personal connection with Al-Sheikh.

“I’m just now getting to know Dana. Seems like a great dude, great businessman. I haven’t heard everything he’s said on all that, but I’m sure he’s thinking about that from a competitive standpoint,” he said. “Boxing is in a great spot. I just want everyone to be successful.

“I got a great team around me, the best in the world at all this,” he said. “I’m focused on my double jab, my defense. I stay in the gym. Never left the gym. So I’m ready for whatever.”
